full_judgment:
Nurul Haque Bhuiyan J: This appeal at the instance of the plaintiff is directed against the judgment and decree dated 27.6.87 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 66 of 1985 and arises out of a suit for declaration that the suit property is not an abandoned property and in the alternative for recovery of possession of the suit property and for realisation of rent or, in the alternative, for mesne profit. 

 5. The learned Subordinate Judge considered the evidence of DW 1 Azizur Rahman, a Deputy Director of the Directorate of Housing, Ministry of Works and the evidence of DW 2 Fazlul Karim, an Office Assistant of the Requisition Branch of Dhaka Collectorate and Ext. A—the requisition order of the suit property, Ext. B — a letter of plaintiff of the year 1976 relating to rent of the suit property, Ext. C-memo of the Estate Officer dated 21.1.77 informing the plaintiff that the suit property was being treated as abandoned property, Ext. 1— a certificate dated 8.5.78 for retirement of the plaintiff from government service issued by MA Hashem, Section Officer, Cabinet Division, Ext. 2—an affidavit sworn on 21.7.72 by the plaintiff before a First Class Magistrate owing allegiance to Bangladesh, Ext. 3—memo of the Ministry of Home dated 27.2.79 addressed to the plaintiff to the effect that the plaintiff did not en-list his name with the International Red Cross for re-turning to Pakistan, Ext. 3(a)—citizenship certificate from First Class Magistrate dated 2.4.73 to the effect that the plaintiff is a citizen of Bangladesh, Ext.3 (b)—passport issued to the plaintiff on 21.6.76, Ext 4—letter of DIT dated 6.9.60 in respect of suit property addressed to the plaintiff, Ext. 4(a)—lease agreement dated 12.11.63 in favour of the plaintiff in respect of the suit property, Ext. 4(b)—receipt of loan petition dated 12.3.69 from House Building Finance Corporation, Ext. 5—the order of requisition dated 14.2.72, Ext. 6 series—petition sent by the plaintiff to the government from 1972 to 1976 for fixation of the rent of the suit property, Ext. 7—memo from the office of Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka dated 20.11.76, Ext.8—Memo of the Estate officer dated 21.1.77 informing the Deputy Commissioner that the suit property was being treated as abandoned property, Ext.9—letter on behalf of the plaintiff to the Estate Officer dated 20.5.77 to make payment of arrear rent in respect of the suit property, Ext. 10—memo of the Estate Officer dated 2.7.77 asking the plaintiff to contact the Ministry of Works for payment of rent in respect of the suit property, Ext. 11—plaintiffs letter dated 7.8.77 to the Secretary, Ministry of Works for release of the suit property. Ext. 12—Memo of the Section Officer, Ministry of Works dated 9.11.77 requesting the plaintiff to appear before him at 10-AM on 19.11.77 with documents in support of his claim, Ext. 12 (a)—plaintiffs letter dated 19.11.77 addressed to the Secretary, Ministry of Works in respect of the release of the suit property, Ext. 12(b)—memo of the Section Officer, Ministry of Works dated 13.12.77 requesting the plaintiff to appear before him at 10 AM on 28.12.77 with documents, Ext 12(c)—memo of the Section Officer, Ministry of Works dated 15.3.78 re-questing the plaintiff to submit two copies of his re-cent passport size photographs, Ext. 12(d)—notice demanding justice dated 4.8.80, Ext. 13—copy of the Writ Petition No. 648/80, Ext. 14—memo of the Section Officer, Ministry of Works dated 3.9.80 to the plaintiffs Advocate Mr. MI Farooqui, Ext.15—letter of plaintiffs Advocate Mr. MI Farooque, dated 6.6.81, Ext. 16—notice demanding justice dated 19.6.81. Ext. 17—copy of the Writ Petition No.540/81 dated 27.7.81, Ext. 17(a)-certified copy of the order dated 27.7.81 in Writ Petition No. 540/81, Ext. 18—plaintiffs letter to the Secretary, Ministry of. Works dated 5.7.82 in respect of release of the suit property, Ext. 19—Findings of the Sub-Divisional Officer (S). Dhaka dated 27.4.83, Ext. 20—Cash deposit by plaintiff dated 6.7.71 in respect of instalment of House Building Finance Corporation, Ext, 21—cash deposit by the plaintiff dated 13.1.77 in respect of ground rent bill, Ext. 22-plaintiffs ration card. Having regard to the findings of the Sub-Divisional Officer (S) to the effect that the plaintiff is a national of this country and his recommendation dated 27.4.83 that the suit property should be released from the list of abandoned property and having considered the citizenship certificate Ext. 3 (a), plaintiffs affidavit Ext. 2, Memo of the Ministry of Home Affairs dated 27.2.79, Ext. 3, plaintiffs passport, Ext. 3(b) and other papers, the learned Subordinate Judge found that the plaintiff is a citizen of this country and he resides in this country. Having regard to the remark of the Process Server on the reverse page of the requisition order dated 14.2.72 Ext.A that the guard of the house received the notice of the requisition order, the learned Subordinate Judge found that the plaintiff was in possession of the suit property. Having regard to the fact that after the requisition on 14.2.72 it was disclosed for the first time in the memo of the Ministry of Public Works dated 21.1.77 Ext. C that the suit property was being treated as abandoned property, the learned Subordinate Judge found that the suit property was never derequisitioned after its requisition in 1972. The learned Subordinate Judge also found that the plaintiff got no scope to file objection as per provisions of the President's Order No. 16 of 1972 and there arose no cause for objection and therefore the plaintiff was entitled to get relief. The suit property having been included in the list of abandoned buildings taken possession under PO No.16/72 published in the official Gazette namely, the Bangladesh Gazette Extra-Ordinary dated 28.4.86 under PO No. 16/ 72 published under section 5(1) (a) of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance, 1985 (Ordinance No. XIV of 1985) the learned Sub-ordinate Judge held the view that the present suit was not maintainable. Accordingly, the learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 27.7.87. Against the decision of the learned Subordinate Judge dated 27.7.87 the plaintiff has preferred this appeal in this court. 

 (a) any decree or order has been passed, at any time before the publication of the list in the official Gazette, by any court declaring the building not to be an abandoned property or not have vested in the Government under the President's Order or declaring the possession by the Government of the building as an abandoned property under that order to be illegal or invalid or directing the Government or any officer or authority subordinate to it to return, restore or transfer the building to any person, or 

 12. In the above circumstances, we hold that the suit property is not an abandoned property and the plaintiff is entitled to get a decree that the suit property is not an abandoned property and a decree for recovery of possession of the suit property and the Government having disclaimed the suit property as requisitioned property and the same having not been found to be an abandoned property as claimed by the Government the Government is liable to restore possession of the suit property to the plaintiff. We further hold that the Government is liable to pay rent/compensation to the plaintiff under the provisions of the East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 for use and occupation of the suit property for the period from 14.2.72 till restoration of possession of the suit property to the plaintiff by the Government. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff-appellant has forgone the plaintiff's claim for mesne profit in respect of the suit property. 

 13. It is found that the judgment and decree of the learned Subordinate Judge suffer from error and illegality as noted above and as such the same call for interference. 

 14. In the result, the appeal is allowed without any order as to costs. The judgment and decree of the learned Subordinate Judge are set aside and the suit is decreed without costs. The plaintiff will be entitled to rent/compensation from the Government under the provisions of East Bengal (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 for Government's use and occupation of the suit property for the period from 14.2.72 till restoration of the suit property to the plaintiff by the Government.
